claims.text: The platform's own recorded distances fix the deviation at 1.60 km: trip_record.actual_distance_km is 8.3 km against trip_record.optimal_distance_km of 6.7 km, and the recommended route ran via Bishan Road / Marymount Road / Thomson Road while the vehicle ran via Braddell Road and Toa Payoh Lorong 6. Under POL-RD-22 the deviation is actual minus optimal, and 1.60 km is above the 1.0 km tolerance, so this is not a within-tolerance trip.

The reroute was not traffic-justified. POL-RD-23 requires traffic data for the recommended route segment at the trip time showing congestion, an incident or a closure. The only advisory in the record covers Marymount Road (the recommended road, from Bishan Road to Thomson Road), overlaps the trip window, and is of type NONE: its own message records no incident, roadwork or closure and speed bands 4-5 throughout. NONE is not one of the types POL-RD-23 recognises, so the advisory does not justify the reroute.

The driver's bare assertion of traffic cannot fill that gap. The counter-statement says Marymount Road 'every morning sure jam one', but POL-RD-23 provides in terms that a driver's assertion of traffic with no supporting data does not justify the reroute, and the advisory that does exist records normal running. There is therefore no traffic justification on this record.

The driver did not inform the rider of the deviation as POL-RD-21 requires. That clause obliges notice by in-app chat, or verbally with the trip call recording as evidence, before or at the point of deviation. The route deviation was detected at 08:16:41, but trip_record.derived.v7.messages_during_trip is empty and the only two chat entries in EV-CHAT-05001 are a pickup-location exchange (MSG-05001-001 and MSG-05001-002) sent at 08:06:32 and 08:07:02, before the trip even started at 08:09:02. Nothing in the chat log touches the route.

Nor can the driver fall back on any verbal notice. trip_record.in_app_calls is empty and no trip call recording is in evidence, and POL-RD-21 read with POL-GEN-26 is explicit that a verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established. The driver's own counter-statement ('Didn't think need to say') confirms no notice was given rather than supplying one.

With the reroute not traffic-justified and the deviation over 1.0 km, POL-RD-24 row (d) applies exactly: refund of the excess distance fare in full. POL-RD-24 arithmetic gives deviation_km x fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd without surge, i.e. 1.60 x 0.72 = 1.152, rounded to 1.15 SGD. fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so nothing has yet been returned to the rider and the whole 1.15 SGD is outstanding.

On the amount I do not overreach: the rider's estimate of 'about $3' is not the policy measure, because POL-RD-24 pays the excess distance fare (1.15 SGD) and not the difference the rider perceived, and no row of the route-deviation matrix returns the whole trip fare. That reduces the figure, not the entitlement: 1.15 SGD is owed, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.15 SGD under POL-GEN-03, not NO_ACTION, which would leave the rider carrying the disputed excess.

This is a case the AI can and should decide on the money rather than hold: the contested value is 3.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence, and the driver profile's fraud_flags is 0 so the 0.95 confidence band is not engaged; POL-RD-25 likewise does not escalate, since the category's 2 km AI-limit limb is not applied and the deviation is 1.60 km in any event. Escalating would only hold the amount, leaving the rider without the 1.15 SGD the matrix owes.

claims.text: The reroute is not traffic-justified, so POL-RD-24 row (d) governs and not rows (a) or (b). The only advisory for the recommended route is EV-ADVIS-05001-01: it sits on Marymount Road (Bishan Road to Thomson Road), it overlaps the trip window, and its type is NONE, its message recording 'No incident, roadwork or closure recorded for the queried segment and window' with speed bands 4-5 throughout. POL-RD-23 requires congestion, an incident or a closure, and it states in terms that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. The driver's counterparty statement that 'Marymount Road every morning sure jam one' is therefore an assertion with no supporting data, and it cannot carry the justification that row (a) or row (b) would need.

The deviation is 1.60 km, measured exactly as POL-RD-22 prescribes on the platform's recorded distances: trip_record.actual_distance_km 8.3 minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km 6.7. The GPS trace is expressly not used to re-measure the distance, because POL-RD-22 says a sparse trace understates a route's length, and the trace here in any event shows the Braddell Road / Toa Payoh Lorong 6 routing rather than the recommended Bishan Road / Marymount Road routing. At 1.60 km the deviation exceeds POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so the within-tolerance rows POL-RD-24(c) and (e) are unavailable and row (d)'s 'over 1 km' limb is satisfied.

The refund is capped at the excess distance fare of 1.15 SGD. POL-RD-24 fixes that figure as the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge: 1.60 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.152, rounded to the cent, 1.15 SGD. The rider's 'about $3' has no basis in the clause, and the other items on the fare breakdown are not part of the route-deviation remedy: the 1.2x surge contributed 2.51 SGD, the time fare 3.78 SGD for 21 minutes, and neither is refundable on a deviation, because POL-RD-24 routes only the excess distance fare back to the rider.

No notice of the deviation was given: the trip record carries no in-app call at all, and its messages_during_trip list is empty, while the chat log's only two entries are pre-pickup logistics sent at 08:06 and 08:07, before the 08:09 trip start and more than seven minutes before the deviation at Bishan Road / Braddell Road. POL-RD-21's notice requirement is therefore not satisfied. That does not enlarge the rider's recovery, however: the row the facts select, POL-RD-24(d), is fixed by the absence of traffic justification and by the excess distance fare, and POL-RD-21 is a precondition of the agreed-deviation row (a) rather than a head of additional refund.

The case can be finally decided now and needs no escalation. The contested amount is 3.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD AI-final band; both profiles carry fraud_flags of 0, so the 0.95 band is not triggered; every artifact in the bundle is COMPLETE at weight 1.0; and POL-RD-25's 2 km limb does not bite because route_deviation.thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false, so the 1.60 km deviation does not force a referral upward. The ruling should be PARTIAL_REFUND limited to the 1.15 SGD excess distance fare, with no driver compensation and no refund of the balance of the fare the rider seeks.
